Why is it not possible to make new types of elementary particles?

In order to make something you need to:

A) build it FROM something

And B) build it USING something

For Making new atoms like plutonium we use uranium as a base and add neutrons using the radioactive decay of the other uranium atoms around it. There is a base (uranium) and something to add (neutrons). All this requires it to be made from something smaller than it.

Elementary particles are as small as it gets. So simply put: there's nothing to make new particles from. As far as we know quarks, leptons, bosons, and electrons are are infinitely small points.
But why it's impossible to make an elementary particle out of available energy and mass that has the same properties as a Z boson but is half as massive?

Where would this mass come from? There is nothing to make a new particle from. Combining these particles only makes something bigger. Neutrons are made up of one up quark and 2 down quark. Mass (and therefore energy) is not even an inherent property of an elementary particle.

One could argue that Man has created elementary particles that are not present naturally: the charmed, beauty and truth quarks, and the tau lepton do not occur at all except when manufactured. (Cosmic rays do produce kaons and lambda baryons, which are strange, and mu-mesons.) There is good cause to believe that there is no fourth set of elementary particles equivalent to the three known generations.

It is suspected that the elementary particles are resonances. Our universe seems to run on wave equations. When a wave travels in a loop, the only stable arrangements have a whole number of wave cycles per loop. For example 2 or 3 cycles, but not something like 2.667381. A whole number of cycles allows the wave to have the same value at the point where the end of the loop meets the beginning, making it an endless cycle.

If this is how things work, then it is simply impossible to create arbitrary particles, for the same reason we cannot create an element between carbon and nitrogen on the periodic table of the elements. The available particles are like keys on a piano whose case we are not allowed to open. And we have to add a zero to the price tag of a particle accelerator every time we want to move one key to the right.
